text: For positive integer m and integers a,b, congruence modulo m means their difference is an integer multiple of m. This yields an equivalence relation on Z with modulus held fixed.
For a fixed positive integer m, two integers are congruent modulo m exactly when Euclidean division by m yields the same remainder in the set {0,1,...,m−1}.

For a square matrix A of order n, its trace is the sum of its diagonal entries indexed from 1 to n. The Einstein summation notation is an alternate notation for this sum, not a distinct contextual meaning.

editorial_note: Harvard-hosted mathematical background §1.2.1, finite-dimensional R^n and explicit empty-hull convention; independently rewritten.
text: On the real space R^d, the affine hull of S comprises finite sums of points of S with real coefficients whose total is exactly one; with S empty, no such combination exists.

editorial_note: Harvard §1.2.1 states smallest affine subspace and the empty-set convention; 'affine-closed' makes the empty convention explicit.
text: The affine hull is the least affine-closed set containing S, equivalently the intersection of all affine-closed supersets of S. Empty S has empty affine hull under the affine-closed-set convention.

editorial_note: ProofWiki main page Definition 2 uses a positive-probability preamble, but its general finite-family definition does not; the pair product-law extension to zero probability is valid.
text: Two measurable events are independent when the probability of their intersection equals the product of their probabilities. The product formula is meaningful even if either event has probability zero.

editorial_note: ProofWiki general definition quantified over all finite index subsets, not just pairs; empty index subset works by P(Omega)=1.
text: An indexed family of measurable events is jointly independent if all its finite subfamilies have intersection probabilities equal to the product of the event probabilities.

editorial_note: ProofWiki explicitly equates the condition with all size-two index subsets, but its symbolic quantifier omits j≠k. Correct distinct-index interpretation adopted; source defect logged as issue.
text: An indexed family of events is pairwise independent when the two-event probability product rule holds for each pair with distinct indices.

editorial_note: ProofWiki's broad circuit/cycle definition allows other graph types and flags the ≥3 restriction for simple graphs; only simple undirected context is admitted here.
text: A cycle in a simple loopless undirected graph can be represented by at least three distinct vertices in cyclic order, with an edge between each consecutive pair including last to first.

editorial_note: ProofWiki explicitly states all three conditions including monotonicity; source-restricted mathematical paraphrase, not lifted wording.
text: An extended nonnegative set function defined on all subsets of X is an outer measure when it vanishes on the empty set, is monotone for inclusion, and is countably subadditive for sequences of subsets.

editorial_note: Encyclopedia of Mathematics article 'Outer measure', Definition 3; cited as a strengthening of standard outer measure, not as independent replacement for its monotonicity condition.
text: For an outer measure on all subsets of a metric space, the metric outer-measure property is additivity for any two subsets whose mutual distance is strictly positive.

editorial_note: ProofWiki Definition 1 of connected topological space; the empty space has no nonempty separation and is thus connected under this convention.
text: A topological space is connected exactly when its underlying set does not split into two disjoint nonempty open sets whose union covers the space.

editorial_note: ProofWiki equivalence article Definition 4 with proof relating no separation to the clopen-set condition; same context, second equivalent formulation.
text: Connectedness of a topological space is equivalent to having no subset that is both open and closed except the empty set and the whole underlying space.

editorial_note: ProofWiki left group action definition, including action order (gh)x=g(hx); left orientation is mathematically different from a right action for nonabelian G.
text: A left action of a group G on a set X is a total assignment G×X to X respecting ordered multiplication of elements of G and the identity action on all x.

editorial_note: ProofWiki right group action definition with explicit order; distinguish from opposite-composition convention and left action.
text: A right action of a group G on a set X is a total assignment X×G to X obeying (xg)h=x(gh) and the right identity law xe=x.
